sources.entry: Codex Account Switcher - Native macOS menu bar app for switching multiple Codex Desktop and CLI accounts and monitoring weekly usage.

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native app for macOS and Windows that switches between multiple saved Codex Desktop accounts and shows weekly usage from a menu bar or tray entry.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you add several Codex accounts through browser sign-in, then select and confirm one in the app. After confirmation it closes Codex Desktop, completes the account handoff, verifies the selected identity, and reopens Desktop. Account rows show weekly allowance by default, with an optional exact 5-hour window, reset counts, and saved subscription dates. The macOS version lives in the menu bar (SwiftUI) and the Windows version uses a WPF window with a system-tray entry (per the README). Saved profiles are stored as local auth.json files in user-only directories. The README says the app has no proxy, traffic router, cloud account service, or automatic account rotation. It is built on a shared Swift 6.2 core, and an npm installer can fetch the desktop app from GitHub Releases.
use_cases: switch between personal and work Codex accounts
switch between client accounts on one Mac or Windows PC
monitor weekly Codex usage per account
menu bar account switching for Codex Desktop
check which Codex account is active before opening Desktop
how_to_run: git clone https://github.com/liuzhao1225/codex-account-switcher (repository URL was blank in the README; clone from the repo name)
notable: Account switch closes Codex Desktop, verifies the selected identity, and reopens Desktop; every switch needs user confirmation
Native macOS menu bar app (macOS 14+, Apple Silicon) and native Windows tray app (Windows 10/11 x64)
Optional codex-reset.com extra-reset forecast shown in the macOS menu bar
Signed and notarized macOS DMG with Sparkle updates; SHA-256 checksums for both platforms
npm installer downloads the latest GitHub release and verifies SHA-256
caveats: Credentials are stored as plain auth.json snapshots protected by file permissions only; backups or snapshots may copy them, and removal is not secure erase
macOS requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14+; Windows requires Windows 10/11 x64; the Windows EXE is currently unsigned
Usage and reset data depend on the Codex usage response; the macOS forecast uses an independent, experimental third-party site and the README says it is not an OpenAI reset schedule
keywords: share one computer between two logins
